note: Re-read RFC 9069 section 5.2 and the current TestHandleBestChangeEmitsPeerUpThenRM after its fixture gained the complete stored four-octet AS_PATH for the same ASN 65001. The collector must read a Peer Up with a nonempty sent OPEN, byte-identical received OPEN, decodable BGP OPEN, the local router-id, ASN4 capability and a family capability before Route Monitoring. Empty OPENs, a different received OPEN, undecodable bytes or lost capabilities fail exact assertions. The single-polarity annotation is valid: ensureLocRIBPeerUp and primeLocRIBPeerUp each build one fabricateLocRIBOpen result and pass that same byte slice to both OPEN fields; there is no separate valid input selecting a received OPEN. The fixture repair changes neither these assertions nor their coverage.
